comparison: Both evaluate histone modification data (C29-C32). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to qualitative analysis and lack of functional data linking acetylation to antimicrobial activity. Peer reviewers accept this characterization work without critique, rating it SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate mammalian/mouse data (C8, C66-C72). Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes lack of functional antibacterial assays. Peer reviewers request toning down claims, note limited experiments, and suggest inappropriate readouts (hepatic injury vs cytokine response) and need for bacterial killing assays.

Both evaluate adult fly data (C7, C51-C54, C75). Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes preliminary characterization and less comprehensive data than embryo studies. Peer reviewers emphasize phenomenon shown only in embryos, limited adult data, and request discussion of adult applicability.

Both address mechanistic claims (C86-C92). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, distinguishing well-supported C86 from speculative mechanism (C87-C92) lacking direct demonstration. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic model without requesting additional validation experiments.

Both evaluate histone identification and antibacterial activity (C3, C22-C28, C33). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from mass spec, antibody blocking, and alkaline carbonate treatment. Peer reviewers describe as 'remarkable new finding' with 'outstanding results,' both rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate histone release mechanism (C1, C2, C62-C65). OpenEval highlights dose-dependent release with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers accept these foundational findings without critique as part of the 'remarkable new finding,' both rating SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate Jabba mutant phenotypes (C34-C38, C42, C98-C101). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing two independent alleles ruling out secondary mutations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting testing in jabba/deficiency background to exclude possible background effects despite independent alleles.

Both evaluate bacterial overgrowth in mutants (C4, C5, C44-C47). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on time-course quantitative data showing clear divergence. Peer reviewers acknowledge large differences but rate UNCERTAIN, requesting additional genetic background testing.

Both evaluate survival data across bacterial species (C6, C43, C48-C50). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing consistent fourfold differences across multiple pathogens with controls. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to concerns about genetic background effects.

Both address the overall mechanism model (C77-C78 in OpenEval; broader mechanism in peer review). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as coherent synthesis of experimental evidence. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the mechanistic model as part of accepted findings, both rating SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates histone degradation (C39-C41) as SUPPORTED with direct experimental evidence and mechanistic interpretation. Peer review R2 includes C39 but focuses on genetic background concerns for the broader mutant phenotype, rating UNCERTAIN.

OpenEval evaluates speculative biological function claims (C73-C74) about maternal transmission and chorion damage as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates evolutionary and regulatory speculation (C80, C93-C97) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are untested hypotheses about trade-offs and cellular regulation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates background/established knowledge claims (C9-C21) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates additional established knowledge claims (C58-C61, C67, C79, C81-C85) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates claims about histone persistence and regulated release (C55-C57) as SUPPORTED, noting experimental validation of initial hypotheses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates citation of prior literature on extracellular histone antibacterial activity (C76) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
